source_meta._title: Screenshot messages aren't prefixed with gray color indicators

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition graphical client running 1.19.1 Pre-release 6. Use a fresh single-player world in Creative mode with cheats enabled and normal command feedback visible. No dedicated server, additional players, seed, resource pack, or datapack is required by the report.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected Java Edition version listed by the report: 1.19.1 Pre-release 6. Do not use the fix version, 1.19.1 Release Candidate 2.
Use the standard graphical game client because the reproduction requires the Take Screenshot control and an on-screen chat overlay.
Create or load a world in which the player has permission to execute /tag. For a deterministic single-player setup, create a Creative-mode world with Allow Cheats enabled.
Leave command feedback enabled so the /tag command produces the system-message control line required by the report.
Ensure chat is not hidden. The chat overlay must be capable of displaying both command feedback and the screenshot-saved message.
If controls have been rebound, identify the key assigned to the Take Screenshot action. Its default key is F2.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher, select an installation that runs Minecraft: Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6, and launch the game.
steps.success_cue: The main menu identifies the running game as 1.19.1 Pre-release 6.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a fresh world. Set Game Mode to Creative and ensure Allow Cheats is enabled, then select Create New World. A specific world seed is not required.
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in the world and can use commands.

steps.action: Wait before continuing until nearby terrain has rendered and player movement and controls respond normally.
steps.success_cue: Surrounding chunks are visible and the client responds normally to movement input.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat control, which is T by default, to place the cursor in the chat input field.
steps.success_cue: The chat interface is open and an input field is ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's tag command into in-game chat exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter to execute it.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and the chat overlay displays feedback confirming that the tag named test was added to the executing player.

steps.action: Use the visible /tag command-feedback line as the control system message. Confirm that its gray color indicator is visible, and do not clear or hide the chat overlay before proceeding.
steps.success_cue: The command-feedback system message remains visible with its gray color indicator, providing a nearby visual reference for the next message.

steps.action: Without leaving the world, invoke the Take Screenshot control once. Press F2 if the default key binding is still in use; otherwise press the key currently bound to Take Screenshot.
steps.success_cue: A screenshot is taken and a screenshot-saved message appears in the in-game chat overlay. Do not assess that message's color indicator yet.

stor.handoff_condition: The Take Screenshot control has just been pressed once, and the resulting screenshot-saved message is visible in the chat overlay near the earlier /tag command-feedback control message. Hand off immediately for visual inspection of the screenshot message.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus multiplayer, game mode, or world seed. A fresh Creative-mode single-player world with cheats enabled is selected as the simplest deterministic setup that permits the supplied command without adding unrelated server conditions.
The report names F2 as the default Take Screenshot control but does not require the binding to remain unchanged; the bound Take Screenshot action is authoritative if controls were remapped.
No web verification was needed because the report supplies the affected version, exact command, trigger action, default screenshot key, and required comparison message.
